purpose: Teach: コック/小鳥/泳ぎ/電球/病室/好き嫌い/真っ直ぐ/昼飯

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、私、レストランで、コックさんに、よく、声、かけていたな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本当に、料理人さんと、お話、するの、好きだったよな、私たち。
lines.en: When I was younger, Gran, do you remember? I used to chat with the chefs at restaurants all the time. We really did love talking with the cooks, didn't we?
lines.style: Soft, reaching backward in time. Opens gently on the memory. Warm and wondering — not quite asking, more like reliving aloud. Pace slows on the chef memories. Ends with genuine affection, not sentimentality.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。庭の餌台、小鳥さんたち、本当に、毎日、来てくれるわよね、あなた、覚えてる、可愛いわよね、私たち、心が、和むわよね、本当に、いつも。
lines.en: Mm-hmm. The little birds come to the feeder in the garden every single day, don't they dear? You remember — aren't they just darling? It really does warm our hearts, doesn't it, always.
lines.style: Contentment with a touch of distraction. She's drifting between the present moment and the small joy she's describing. Rhythmic, almost soothing cadence. Repeats warmly, like tending something living.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、海で、泳ぎ、得意だったわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?毎年、夏、二人で、よく、海に、行ったよな、本当に、楽しかったよな、本当に、思い出。
lines.en: When I was young, I was quite the swimmer, wasn't I Gran? Do you remember? Every summer the two of us would go to the sea so often. It was really such fun, wasn't it — such a memory.
lines.style: Nostalgic pull, but with a slight ache underneath. Opens on the younger self. Pace quickens a touch as he lists the summers, then softens on 'memory.' The question marks are genuine reaching, not rhetorical.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 電球の取り替え、最近、息子に、頼むようになっちゃったわよね、あなた、年取って、危ないこと、しないようにしましょうね、お互いに、本当に、健康、第一。
lines.en: Changing light bulbs — well, I've been asking our son to do it lately, haven't I dear? Now that we're getting on, we shouldn't be doing dangerous things, should we? We have to look after each other. Health comes first, really.
lines.style: A gentle pivot to present practicality. Not sorrowful, but grounded and caring. She's speaking sense without lecturing. Warm but matter-of-fact. The repeated 'really' lands with quiet certainty, not emphasis.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: お祖母ちゃんが、入院されてた病室、ばあさん、覚えてる?お見舞いに、毎日、行ったわよな、私たち、本当に、心配したわよな、本当に、辛い時期だった。
lines.en: Do you remember when your grandmother was in the hospital, Gran? We went to visit her every day, didn't we? We were so worried about her — it was such a difficult time, really.
lines.style: Tender but with an undercurrent of pain. He's present with the memory, not lost in it. Opens quietly. Pace steadies on the difficult parts — he doesn't rush through the hurt. Ends with acceptance, not resignation.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 孫、好き嫌い、最近、減ってきたわよね、あなた、お祖母ちゃん、本当に、嬉しいわよ、お野菜、ちゃんと、食べてるって、聞いて、安心したわよね、本当に。
lines.en: Our grandchild's been getting pickier about food less and less lately, haven't they dear? Grandmother's so happy about that — I was so relieved when I heard they were eating their vegetables properly, you know. Really.
lines.style: Genuine delight mixed with quiet relief. She's reporting good news about someone she loves. Rhythmic, almost singing the words. The relief is real and sits under the joy. Warm and present throughout.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔、私たち、真っ直ぐな道、二人で、よく、歩いたわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?夕暮れの散歩、本当に、ロマンチックだったよな、本当に、思い出すよ、いつも。
lines.en: A long time ago, the two of us used to walk down that straight road together so often, didn't we Gran? Do you remember? The evening walks were so romantic, weren't they? I still think about them, always.
lines.style: Deep affection. He's walking through the memory as he speaks it. Opens with certainty, not question. Slows on 'romantic' — lets it linger. The final 'always' is quiet, almost to himself. A man still in love with the past they shared.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 今日のお昼飯、お祖父ちゃん、何が、食べたい?ばあさん、何でも、作ってあげるわよ、リクエスト、教えてね、本当に、嬉しいわよ、料理、するの、ね。
lines.en: What would you like for lunch today, Grandpa? Grandmother will make anything you want, dear. Just tell me what you'd like — I'm so happy to cook for you, you know, really.
lines.style: Immediate, present warmth. She shifts into caretaker mode with joy, not duty. Opens bright. There's anticipation in her voice — she wants to please him. 'Anything' lands with genuine generosity. Repeats 'really' with the pleasure of doing this small thing.
